nodes.description: The disease variants do not act uniformly. Some reduce steady-state CCTalpha abundance in patient fibroblasts; others leave the protein present but impair phosphatidylcholine synthesis. In vitro, catalytic-domain missense variants aggregate irrecoverably, several destabilise the catalytic fold with measurable substrate Km defects, and one autoinhibitory-helix deletion paradoxically increases constitutive activity. That heterogeneity is why the same gene yields three different diseases.

evidence.reference_title: Disease-linked mutations in the phosphatidylcholine regulatory enzyme CCTα impair enzymatic activity and fold stability.
evidence.snippet: Previous analyses showed that for some disease-linked PCYT1A variants steady state levels of CCTα and PC synthesis were reduced in patient fibroblasts, but other variants impaired PC synthesis with little effect on CCT levels.

evidence.reference_title: Disease-linked mutations in the phosphatidylcholine regulatory enzyme CCTα impair enzymatic activity and fold stability.
evidence.snippet: Five variants destabilized the catalytic domain-fold as assessed by lower transition temperatures for unfolding, and three of these manifested defects in substrate Km values.

nodes.description: A cone-rod dystrophy causing progressive visual impairment. It is the feature that names the disorder and the one that separates it from every other spondylometaphyseal dysplasia except the PLCB3-related form, which has corneal rather than retinal disease.

evidence.reference_title: Defect in phosphoinositide signalling through a homozygous variant in PLCB3 causes a new form of spondylometaphyseal dysplasia with corneal dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: Cone rod dystrophy is a feature of SMDCRD which is caused by loss-of-function variants in PCYT1A.

nodes.description: Progressive cone-rod retinal dystrophy causing visual impairment; the defining extra-skeletal feature.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in PCYT1A cause spondylometaphyseal dysplasia with cone-rod dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: Spondylometaphyseal dysplasia with cone-rod dystrophy is a rare autosomal-recessive disorder characterized by severe short stature, progressive lower-limb bowing, flattened vertebral bodies, metaphyseal involvement, and visual impairment caused by cone-rod dystrophy.

nodes.description: Metaphyseal involvement with flattened vertebral bodies, producing severe short stature and progressive bowing of the lower limbs.

nodes.description: Reduced synthesis of phosphatidylcholine, the most abundant membrane phospholipid. CCTalpha is itself membrane-sensing - it is activated by binding phosphatidylcholine-deficient membranes - so the enzyme normally sits in a feedback loop that maintains membrane composition, and a defective enzyme breaks that homeostatic loop rather than simply lowering output.

nodes.description: No disease-modifying treatment exists. Management is supportive: low-vision support for the retinal dystrophy, orthopaedic management of the bowing and short stature.

evidence.snippet: Thus, the deregulation of the phosphatidylcholine pathway may play a role in multiple genetic diseases in humans, and further studies are necessary to uncover its precise pathogenic mechanisms and the entirety of its phenotypic spectrum.

evidence.reference_title: Disease-linked mutations in the phosphatidylcholine regulatory enzyme CCTα impair enzymatic activity and fold stability.
evidence.snippet: Mutations in the gene encoding CCTα (PCYT1A) cause three distinct pathologies in humans: lipodystrophy, spondylometaphyseal dysplasia with cone-rod dystrophy (SMD-CRD), and isolated retinal dystrophy.
